newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes down on weak fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes down on weak fundamentals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed lower Wednesday amid continued bearish market fundamentals, trade souces said Wednesday.
"We ran up over the past couple of days on short-term unit outages, but apparently everyone realized they were short-term. We gave up those gains today," said one trader.
In addition, the market returned its focus to this year's abundant hydropower outlook, "not only in the Northwest, but also in California," he said.
"It's been pretty cold in the Southwest, plus some units are out, but (daily) Palo Verde prices didn't break $17.00 (per megawatt hour)," said another dealer.
"July starting looking expensive at $20.00," he added.
July Palo Verde closed down 50 cents at $19.95 per megawatt hour (MWh), while the May contract lost 25 cents to close at $13.75 and April was down 20 cents at $12.90.
California-Oregon border (COB) futures also lost ground, with April down 57 cents at $9.38, May down 60 cents at $9.40 and June 30 cents lower at $10.45.
Traders said prices were down another 5 to 10 cents in late over-the-counter trade on Wednesday and could continue trading lower on Thursday.
"The fundamentals are still bearish. I didn't see too many bids at the end of the day," said one trader.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average one to four degrees Fahrenheit below normal for the next several days, with above-normal precipitation seen through the weekend.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to average about four degrees below normal through the weekend, with above-normal precipitation seen during the same period.
NYMEX estimated 201 COB and 224 PV contracts traded on Wednesday.
